sections.content: When you describe someone with an adjective or a profession, Hungarian drops *van* in the 3rd person: *Anna magas* (Anna is tall), *Károly orvos* (Károly is a doctor). But when you say WHERE something or someone is, *van/vannak* can never be dropped — this is one of the most important distinctions to keep in mind in descriptive writing, such as introducing a country.

to spread out, to extend (of a region or landscape)

items.english: The country lies in the Carpathian Basin.

items.spanish: Budapest a Duna két partján van.
items.english: Budapest is on both banks of the Danube.

sections.content: *Magyarország szép* (no *van*) describes a quality, so *van* disappears in the 3rd person — but *Magyarország Közép-Európában van* states a LOCATION, and here *van* is compulsory. *fekszik* and *elterül* are not new grammar, just more formal synonyms for *van* that historical and geographic writing prefers — you'll see them throughout this unit's readings.
